create.title: Reciprocal Fourier modes and exponent-pair capacity of unmatched crossings
create.statement_tex: For J=sqrt(X), T=sqrt(X/N), Q=J/T, and fixed Xi, the floor-compatible Vaaler main of the Round-65 discrepancy has modes S_k(v)=sum_j chi_4(j)Xi(j/J)e(k floor(X)/j)(1-e(kv/j)) with coefficient O(1/|k|), plus the difference of two positive Fejer residuals. The exact wavelet filter localizes nonzero main modes to |k| asymp Q. A lawful exponent pair (kappa,lambda) therefore has capacity J^lambda Q^kappa=X^((lambda+kappa nu)/2+epsilon). At nu=2/5, TTY gives 5163/12820 and the classical pair (2/7,4/7) gives 12/35, both worse than the trivial product exponent 3/10. The residual satisfies sum_(j asymp J)E_K(n/j)<<X^epsilon(1+J/K), hence is target-safe for K>=X^(1/4). A new joint signed (j,k) theorem with lossless off-diagonal control is required.
create.next_action: Formulate a joint signed j-k large-sieve or bilinear off-diagonal theorem whose diagonal is exactly X^(1/4) and whose off-diagonal loses no power.

update.next_action: One-variable exponent pairs are weaker than the original product bound. Attack the joint j-k off-diagonal at an exactly target-sized diagonal, while retaining the Fejer residual and full-cone scope.
The separable test case now needs a lossless joint reciprocal-mode off-diagonal theorem; one-variable exponent pairs do not gain H/L.

reject.reason: At nu=2/5 the exact wavelet transition capacity is X^(5163/12820+epsilon), worse than both the target and the original trivial product bound.
Exact wavelet averaging uses the difference factor to localize k asymp J/T; it does not leave an additional independent small factor after resummation.
At an integer the floor-compatible residual has magnitude one half; divisor grouping, not deletion, yields the bound X^epsilon(1+J/K).
The cited trilinear theorem requires modular inverses and coprimality, unlike the ordinary phase e(kX/j) with moving difference amplitude.

no_change.reason: No joint signed reciprocal-mode theorem or full-cone estimate is proved.
Round 66 proves a reduction and capacity no-go, not an exponent.

round_assessment.reason: Round 66 identifies the exact transition-frequency and proves that every audited one-variable exponent-pair route loses to the original trivial bound; the required joint off-diagonal remains open.
